hooks.text: A car-sized robot is climbing a mountain taller than Mount Everest.
Can a car-sized robot climb a mountain taller than Mount Everest?
This Martian mountain rises taller from base to peak than Mount Everest.

title: The Martian Mountain Taller Than Mount Everest
description: In the center of Gale Crater on Mars, Aeolis Mons towers higher than Mount Everest from base to peak. For over a decade, NASA's Curiosity rover has been slowly climbing its slopes.

beats.text: A car-sized robot is climbing a mountain taller than Mount Everest.
beats.visual: Curiosity rover selfie on the slopes of Mount Sharp, 2015

beats.text: This is Aeolis Mons, an enormous central peak rising inside Mars's Gale Crater.
beats.visual: Orbital view of Gale Crater and Aeolis Mons on Mars, 2012

beats.text: At five point five kilometers tall, this Martian giant easily dwarfs Seattle's Mount Rainier.
beats.visual: Scenic view of Mount Rainier from Seattle, 2020

beats.text: In fact, its vertical rise from base to peak is greater than Mount Everest's.
beats.visual: Photograph of Mount Everest base-to-peak rise, 2018

beats.text: This mountain consists of ancient sedimentary layers, eroded over billions of years by Martian winds.
beats.visual: Layered sandstone formations at Murray Buttes on Mars, 2016

beats.text: In August 2012, NASA's car-sized Curiosity rover landed inside the wide crater basin.
beats.visual: Artist's illustration of Curiosity Sky Crane descent onto Mars, 2012

beats.text: Using its robotic drill, Curiosity discovered organic chemicals locked inside these ancient lakebed layers.
beats.visual: Curiosity robotic arm showing instrument turret on Martian rock, 2014

beats.text: To investigate if Mars once supported life, this tireless, car-sized robot is still climbing.
beats.visual: Curiosity rover looking up toward Mount Sharp summit, 2021
